text:
Emma: quick sync — can we spell out a minimal, actionable split of oncall responsibilities between SRE and Runtime? Doing a handoff later and want the notes to be clear for non-incident coverage (FYI / risk flags, who to page, what to own).

Raj: +1. Runtime owns model serving surface: model binary rollouts, in-process KV cache correctness, model-specific fallbacks (e.g., smaller model variants), and per-request routing logic. For any model-induced quality regressions we triage first in runtime.

Lina: SRE owns infra-level stuff: node health, autoscaler, networking (VPCs, peering), cloud provider incidents, and the platform-level monitoring/alerting. If it's a cloud region outage or node OOM we take primary.

Emma: can we add a short escalation path? i.e., when runtime pings SRE and vice versa. Also want a clear 'definition of incident' we can paste into the handoff note.

Raj: escalation (short):
- Level 0 (FYI): degraded quality or a single-model tail latency spike — ping the channel + @oncall-runtime, add a short note to runbook.
- Level 1 (action): sustained latency regression or >5% error rate across requests — page SRE if autoscaling or infra looks suspicious, otherwise runtime leads mitigation (rollback/patch).
- Level 2 (critical): total outage, cross-region failures, or security incident — page both SRE and Runtime primary pagers, follow incident playbook.

Lina: definition proposal: "Incident = any event that materially impacts customer-facing SLA (latency, availability, correctness) or exposes sensitive data." For handoffs we treat anything that might impact >1% of requests or any PII issue as incident-level.

Matt: +1 from infra. Also add: if alert points to node-level metrics (CPU/VM/driver errors), SRE owns host remediation and will coordinate with runtime for rolling restarts/evacuations.

Emma: good. Two more practical items for the handoff note:
1) Who owns the short-term mitigation (rollback vs. autoscaler tweak)
2) Who updates the oncall postmortem template when it's non-incident but we had a risky handoff

Raj: (1) runtime leads rollback/feature-flag flips; SRE can do capacity maneuvers if it's clearly infra. (2) if it's non-incident risky handoff, the person who initiated the handoff files a 1-paragraph note in the runbook; if it triggered an operational change, create a short post with the "oncall-impact" tag and assign to engineering owner.

Lina: adding runbook checklist suggestion:
- current capacity and autoscaler status
- recent deploys and model rollouts (last 24h)
- any known flaky infra alerts and mitigations tried
- contact matrix (pager + slack + backup)

Oncall Bot: Handoff saved by Emma at 2026-03-16 22:14 UTC. Reminder: attach runbook link when handing off.

Emma: I'll draft the handoff note now and link to the runbook. Would one of you review quickly? @Raj @Lina :eyes:

Raj: happy to review. Please add the escalation bullets to the runtime runbook page.

Lina: I can add the infra checklist to the SRE runbook after your draft.

Emma: thanks — I'll ping when done. Short-term action: include rollback command snippet and the pager list in the handoff.

Raj: snippet for rollback (example):
```
# rollback last model rollout
redwoodctl serve rollback --service=model-runtime --to-version=2026-03-15-2
```

Emma: perfect. saved in the draft. Closing loop — will post the final handoff note in this thread when ready. :white_check_mark:
